- **self**: LoRA adapters in Ollama via ADAPTER (8/4)

## Structure and components

- [statement] The current docs.ollama.com import page covers only whole-model Safetensors and GGUF import and shows no adapter workflow. The current Modelfile reference source (docs/modelfile.mdx on main) contains no occurrence of 'adapter' or 'lora'. The only documented ADAPTER guidance found is in the older 0.9.0 guide. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://docs.ollama.com/import · keywords: LoRA adapters in Ollama via ADAPTER · also: https://docs.ollama.com/modelfile

## How it works

- [statement] Ollama's guide advises non-quantized (non-QLoRA) adapters, because most frameworks use different quantization methods. (low confidence) — https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ollama/ollama@0.9.0/docs/import.md · keywords: LoRA adapters in Ollama via ADAPTER

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] To import a Safetensors LoRA adapter, write a Modelfile with FROM <base model name> and ADAPTER /path/to/safetensors/adapter/directory, then run ollama create. ADAPTER . works when the adapter sits beside the Modelfile. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ollama/ollama@0.9.0/docs/import.md · keywords: LoRA adapters in Ollama via ADAPTER · also: https://docs.ollama.com/import

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Merging a PEFT LoRA into a quantized base re-quantizes the base weight, so repeated merge/unmerge cycles accumulate rounding error; for deployment prefer one merge_and_unload() (assign the returned model) and keep the unmerged adapter, which supports merging offline before an Ollama FROM import as an alternative to ADAPTER. (medium confidence) — https://huggingface.co/docs/peft/main/en/developer_guides/lora · keywords: LoRA adapters in Ollama via ADAPTER · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/tools/export-lora/README.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The FROM base must be the same base model used to train the adapter. Otherwise results are erratic. The same rule is stated for GGUF adapters. (low confidence) — https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ollama/ollama@0.9.0/docs/import.md · keywords: LoRA adapters in Ollama via ADAPTER
- [statement] Per the 0.9.0 import guide, Safetensors adapters are supported for Llama (2, 3, 3.1, 3.2), Mistral (1, 2, Mixtral) and Gemma (1, 2) architectures. Adapters can be produced by Hugging Face training, Unsloth or MLX. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ollama/ollama@0.9.0/docs/import.md · keywords: LoRA adapters in Ollama via ADAPTER
- [statement] For a GGUF adapter, write FROM <model name> and ADAPTER /path/to/file.gguf. FROM may be an Ollama model, a GGUF file or a Safetensors model. A GGUF adapter comes from llama.cpp's convert_lora_to_gguf.py or a download such as Hugging Face. (low confidence) — https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ollama/ollama@0.9.0/docs/import.md · keywords: LoRA adapters in Ollama via ADAPTER
- [statement] llama.cpp ships an export-lora tool that applies one or more LoRA adapters (--lora, comma-separated, or --lora-scaled FNAME:SCALE) to a base model and writes a merged GGUF, f16 by default. This is an alternative to ADAPTER: merge offline, then import the merged file with plain FROM. (low confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/tools/export-lora/README.md · keywords: LoRA adapters in Ollama via ADAPTER
